why: Note: the words "except that the directors of Blinded Veterans Association, Incorporated, on August 27, 1958 shall be the first directors of the corporation" are omitted as executed and obsolete.
Note: the renaming words "on and after August 10, 1964, as the United States Olympic Committee" are omitted as executed; the reference rule survives in 220502(c).

Note: "which has been or may after June 26, 1946, be" is omitted as obsolete (2103) and "on or after July 25, 1956" is omitted as obsolete (2110); the flagged 122-132 are section cross-references replaced by "this chapter".
Note: the words "occurring ... on or after January 1, 1964" are omitted as obsolete.
Note: the words "On and after June 20, 1878" are omitted as obsolete.

Note: "fined under title 18" is substituted for the $5,000 felony fine and the $500 misdemeanor fine "for consistency with chapter 227 of title 18"; the other numbers are old section cross-references renumbered.
Note: the $500,000, the FY1939-1948 $200,000 a year, the July 8, 1937 words and the FY1938 $10,000 are omitted as obsolete and replaced by "Necessary amounts are appropriated for the fund".

The restatement kept $750,000,000 and the two-program limit; the edition compared already includes Pub. L. 107-314 and 107-347 (Dec. 2002), which per the Amendments note removed (b)(1) and cut the cap to $375,000,000.

Note: "amounts authorized to be expended from the Fund" is substituted for "this authorization, and hereafter" to restate the provision as general and permanent law, so the October 21, 1998 start date drops out.
Note: "The text of 40:871(a)-(e) is omitted as obsolete"; the 1935 and 1965 dates were only in those findings, and the boundary description is kept in full.
Note: "in the case of any contract entered into after October 9, 1940" is omitted as obsolete, and the "heretofore since July 1, 1950, or hereafter" words are cut "to eliminate unnecessary words".
Note: 41:358(1)-(4) (FY1973-1976 thresholds of 25/20/15/10 employees) and "On and after July 1, 1976" are omitted as obsolete; the standing threshold of more than 5 employees is kept in 6707(f).
Note: "chapter 309 or 311 of title 46" is substituted for the Act of March 9, 1920 and the Act of March 3, 1925 because those Acts were themselves restated in title 46, so the same law is cited.
Note: in 1303(b)(1)(A) "the words 'after 60 days after November 17, 1988' are omitted as obsolete".
Note: "The words 'On and after September 5, 1962' are omitted as obsolete."
The disposition table lists "2465a(b) Rep."; that subsection was the one-time implementation plan due within six months of November 16, 1990, which had long been executed.
The new text still says "up to 100 percent"; note: "up to 100 percent" is substituted for "100 percent, or any lesser percent" to eliminate unnecessary words.
Note: "Every 2 years" is substituted for "Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act [December 30, 2005], and every 2 years thereafter" to eliminate obsolete language.
The disposition table lists "17812(b) Elim."; it was a one-time review due 18 months after October 15, 2008 (April 2010), which had passed before the December 2010 restatement.
The notes say nothing, but October 17, 1998 was the source Act's own enactment date and "designation by law after" that date has no remaining effect, so dropping it is surplus and not substantive.

The table sends the penalty words to "See §4(a)(1) of bill" (18 U.S.C. 1865), and 100751(c) is "added for informational purposes"; the $500 fine becomes the general title 18 fine there (the 1865 text is not in the cache, so this is unverified).
Note: "The words 'within 1 year after November 2, 1994' are omitted as obsolete."

The table maps all of 1a-2(g) to 101702, but 101702(c) keeps only the living-exhibit sale; the Glacier Bay rules (60% of permit fees to a special account, the $5-per-passenger fee cap, the 500-passenger/3-night definition, the limits on operating conditions) appear nowhere in title 54 (2014 or 2024), and the 101702 notes say nothing.

national parks and national monuments which on August 25, 1916, were under the jurisdiction of the Department of the Interior is folded into the defined term "System units", which covers them; the notes explain only the Hot Springs omission and say nothing about the date.
